questions.prompt: Using the model for Entropy Production, Irreversibility, and the Arrow of Time, set up the governing equation, inequality, derivative, probability, or phase-rule count and solve the following problem: A quantity \(Q=600\,\mathrm{J}\) passes from a body at \(T_H=400\,\mathrm{K}\) to one at \(T_C=300\,\mathrm{K}\), while both temperatures remain effectively constant. Find the entropy generation of the isolated two-body composite.
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Entropy Production, Irreversibility, and the Arrow of Time under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
Equation \([5]\) gives \[S_{\mathrm{gen}}=\Delta S_{\mathrm{isolated}}=600\left(\frac{1}{300}-\frac{1}{400}\right)\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}=0.500\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}.\] The hot body changes by \(-1.50\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\), the cold body by \(+2.00\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\), and their sum is positive. Final result: \(S_{\mathrm{gen}}=0.500\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\), confirming irreversible hot-to-cold transfer.

Final answer:
\(S_{\mathrm{gen}}=0.500\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\), confirming irreversible hot-to-cold transfer.
